features.title: What it does
features.boardroom:
AI Boardroom

Decisions run as isolated multi-perspective debates with critic cross-examination and synthesis, across 80 frameworks from OKR to Pre-Mortem.
features.omniroute:
OmniRoute cost control

A central switchboard routes every request to local (Ollama, LM Studio) or cloud models. Budgets are checked before dispatch and attributed per model and per task.
features.zeroEgress:
Zero-Egress & GDPR / DSGVO

Finance, HR, contract, and CRM data stays on local models inside an isolated Docker network with no internet route. Fails closed when enabled - Zero-Egress is off by default and can be activated with local models or EU-based providers.
features.audit:
Audit Log, EU AI Act & GoBD

A SHA-256 hash-chained log records every dispatch (provider, model, host) tamper-evidently, paired with an EU AI Act risk registry and 1-click GoBD procedural documentation export.
features.obsidian:
Obsidian vault + RAG

Your vault is the knowledge base. Documents and scans are OCR-read, converted to Markdown and indexed into AnythingLLM/Chroma - locally.
features.kanban:
Kanban with approval gates

Tasks move through a four-eyes gate: approve, reject with a reason, or escalate on expiry. Email triage, CRM and an ERP suite (alpha) sit on top.
features.liveness:
24/7 monitoring

A heartbeat reports a stall immediately (/livez returns 503) and restarts hung services. An external watchdog can raise an additional alarm.
features.hardened:
Hardened & traced

SSRF and prompt-injection guards, distributed trace IDs across agent calls, and batched UI rendering for large prompt catalogs.
features.telegram:
Telegram, Email & CRM

Triage incoming emails and Telegram messages into Kanban tasks, sync contacts, and manage quotes and contracts in one workspace.
features.passkey:
Passkey / WebAuthn HITL (per user)

Once a user registers a passkey (config/passkey_hitl.json), high-risk approvals (payments, budget overruns, destructive actions) require a cryptographic signature via Windows Hello, Touch ID or a hardware passkey. Without registration the feature is off for that user — enable it before relying on it in production.
features.budgetbank:
Atomic BudgetBank & Signed Warrants

Token and cost budgets are reserved transactionally before execution (BEGIN IMMEDIATE). Privileged tools require time-bound HMAC-SHA256 warrants.
features.ledger:
No duplicate actions

External effects are recorded before dispatch and reconciled after a crash. A payment is not executed twice.

why.title: Why Archon OS?
why.text: Built for commercial accountability and GDPR/DSGVO compliance, not toy demos. Unlike prompt-chaining libraries that leave cost caps, data egress, and compliance boundaries to custom glue code, Archon OS includes Atomic BudgetBank reservations, WebAuthn Passkey approvals, EU AI Act / GoBD documentation, and SHA-256 audit trails - Zero-Egress is off by default - on 3 consolidated SQLite WAL databases (ops.db, business.db, memory.db). Zero-Egress is off by default and must be enabled with local models (see settings.json: privacy.zero_egress, zero_egress_strict).
faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.what:
What is Archon OS?

Archon OS is a self-hosted, MIT-licensed Agentic Operating System built on Hermes Agent. It organizes 71 specialist AI roles across 8 domains with pre-execution budget reservations, Zero-Egress local LLM routing, WebAuthn Passkey approvals, and a SHA-256 hash-chained audit log.
faq.leaks:
How does it prevent sensitive data leaks?

OmniRoute enforces a fail-closed Zero-Egress policy: finance, contracts, CRM, HR, and GDPR workloads run exclusively on local models (Ollama or LM Studio) inside an internal Docker network without an internet route. Fail-closed applies only when enabled; the shipped default is privacy.zero_egress = false.
faq.costs:
How are token costs & risky actions controlled?

A central PolicyEngine validates permissions before dispatch, privileged tools require signed time-bound warrants, BudgetBank reserves funds atomically, and high-risk approvals require WebAuthn Passkey signatures.
faq.gdpr:
Is it GDPR (DSGVO) & EU AI Act ready?

Compliance depends on your configuration. Sensitive business workloads stay on your server with fail-closed Zero-Egress, backed by an EU AI Act risk registry, tamper-evident SHA-256 audit logs, and 1-click GoBD procedural documentation export.
status.title: Honest status
status.text: Pre-1.0. Interfaces and config keys change between releases. The ERP/CRM module is alpha, multi-user role enforcement is still being hardened, and specialist output is decision support, not licensed advice. Issues and PRs are welcome. Authentication: the shipped settings.json has no auth block; on 127.0.0.1 Archon OS runs as a local single-user. Set auth.enabled = true before LAN or production use.

faq.chatbot:
How is Archon OS different from a regular chatbot?

A chatbot answers. Archon OS enforces: budget gates before every model call, passkey approvals for high-risk actions, and a verifiable audit trail. The difference is enforcement, not conversation.
b2b.section:
Built for regulated environments

Procurement: supplier comparisons and contract drafts run behind passkey approvals; budget caps stop uncontrolled agent spend. Controlling: every dispatch is logged with provider, model and cost in a hash-chained trail — one-click GoBD export. Compliance: TOM matrix, EU AI Act risk register and a consent gate under § 201 StGB (confidentiality of speech) are configuration, not add-ons.

Economics: €0 licence (MIT). You own infrastructure, configuration and operation; Zero-Egress is explicitly an option, not a guarantee.

Scope limitation (honest status): Zero-Egress is off by default and must be enabled with local models or EU providers. The ERP/CRM module is alpha and multi-user role enforcement is still being hardened. Agent output is decision support, not licensed advice. Full status →
